newsitem.title: MEXICO: Family and friends mourn Mexico's "Lord of Skies".
newsitem.headline: Family and friends mourn Mexico's "Lord of Skies".

text.p: A grieving family and a horde of peasant hangers-on mourned Mexico's top drug lord on Friday as officials investigated a report that he was murdered in his hospital bed last week by an overdose of medicine.
A local priest led a Catholic mass on Friday morning for dead cocaine king Amado Carrillo Fuentes inside the luxury northwestern Mexican ranch belonging to his mother Aurora.

As tears streamed down the faces of relatives and friends, mourners sang a song based on the parable of the lost sheep from St. Luke's Gospel. "There is more rejoicing in the heavens for one sinner who repents than for 99 just men who do not need to repent", the words ran.

Carrillo Fuentes' three sisters, clad in black and laden with gold jewellery, had sat up all night wailing at the grey metallic coffin containing the decomposing body of their brother, who died seven days ago in mysterious circumstances.
"He always said they'd never get him alive," sister Alicia Carrillo Fuentes told Reuters. She recalled a conversation with her mother about Amado a couple of years earlier.
"When I asked about him, Mama said: 'That's what he does and God will look after him'", Alicia said.

A heavy army and police presence outside the family ranch in the farming village of Guamuchilito, about 600 miles (1,000 km) northwest of Mexico City, appeared to have kept many mobster associates away.
Cars entering the Guamuchilito ranch were searched by soldiers backed by a light armoured vehicle and their occupants were videotaped.
Soldiers said the checks were routine searches for firearms but many suspected the troops were hunting Carrillo's brothers, who are possible heirs to the leadership of his Juarez cartel.
As mourners waited to bury the body the trickle of guests early on turned into a flood, some driving in aboard brand new four wheel drive vehicles.

Journalists were discouraged from leaving the compound in a bid to prevent it from being stormed by soldiers as it was during a Carrillo Fuentes family wedding in January. On that occasion the drug lord gave soldiers the slip after receiving a tipoff they were coming after him.

In Mexico City, investigators said they were checking a report that Carrillo Fuentes died after one of the men accompanying him for his plastic surgery and liposuction operation ordered nurses to slip a drug named "Dormicum" into his intravenous drip against doctors' orders.

Reforma newspaper said on Friday, quoting medical sources, that duty nurses protested as the men ordered the dose of "Dormicum" in the early hours of the morning. The report said the drug stopped his heart and breathing.
Medics treating him had explicitly forbidden any such treatment, as they did not want him given any additional medication after his surgery, it added.
"It's not possible to be sure whether they killed him or not," said Mexico's top anti-drug agent Mariano Herran Salvatti in a radio interview. "We still can't determine the cause of death."
Family sources told Reuters they expected the "Lord of the Skies" to be laid to rest in front of the ranch's private grey marble chapel in the early evening.
Friends said the durg lord's mother Aurora was furious at authorities for first delaying the handover of the body, then disrupting the wake and funeral preparations.
Although U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration officials identified the body on Sunday, Mexican authorities waited until Thursday evening to confirm Carrillo Fuentes' death.
U.S. officials considered Carrillo Fuentes the most important figure in the Mexican drug trade, shipping tons of cocaine a year to the United States from his base in northern Mexico.
Carrillo Fuentes was head of the Juarez drug cartel and earned his nickname from the huge air shipments of Colombian cocaine he flew to Mexico and smuggled across the United States border.
